subject: Kobe Bryant

facts.text: Last NBA game: 60 points, Apr 13, 2016 vs. Utah (22-50 FG, 6 threes, 10-12 FT, W), at 37 years, 234 days old.
facts.why: The greatest farewell box score there is; post it on the anniversary.

facts.text: Regular-season career high: 81 points, Jan 22, 2006 vs. Toronto (28-46 FG, 7 threes, 18-20 FT, W).
facts.why: One of the most famous box scores in the sport; every detail gets shared.

facts.text: Playoff career high: 50 points, May 4, 2006 vs. Phoenix (20-35 FG, 5 threes, 5-6 FT, L).
facts.why: The ceiling game; the box score details are the post.

facts.text: Bryant played 1,346 regular-season and 220 playoff games, scoring 33,643 and 5,640 points — 39,283 in all.
facts.why: The career in one line; the combined total is the number fans rarely see.

facts.text: Longest run of consecutive regular-season games with 40+ points: 9 (Feb 6, 2003 to Feb 23, 2003).
facts.why: Hot-streak content is the most shareable kind of scoring stat.

facts.text: Longest run of consecutive regular-season games with 50+ points: 4 (Mar 16, 2007 to Mar 23, 2007).
facts.why: Hot-streak content is the most shareable kind of scoring stat.
Rings are the first thing every GOAT debate cites.

facts.text: When he retired after 2015-16, only Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Karl Malone had scored more regular-season points (33,643).
facts.why: All-time rank at retirement is the legacy stat.

facts.text: 40-point regular-season games: Bryant 122, Jordan 173.
facts.why: The comparison fans argue about most, settled with a count.

facts.text: 50-point regular-season games: Bryant 25, Jordan 31.
facts.why: Fifty-point games, head to head; guaranteed replies from both camps.

facts.text: First NBA game: 0 points, Nov 3, 1996 vs. Minnesota, at 18 years, 72 days old.
facts.why: Origin-story content; the age on the debut is the hook.

facts.text: Bryant played all 1,346 of his regular-season games for the Lakers — 20 seasons with one franchise.
facts.why: One-franchise loyalty is rare and a point of pride for that fan base.

facts.text: 50-point regular-season games: 25 (2% of his regular-season games).
facts.why: Fifty-point games are the scorer's trophy case; the count is instantly comparable.

facts.text: 60-point regular-season games: 6 — 62 Dec 20, 2005 vs. Dallas; 81 Jan 22, 2006 vs. Toronto; 65 Mar 16, 2007 vs. Portland; 60 Mar 22, 2007 at Memphis; 61 Feb 2, 2009 at New York; 60 Apr 13, 2016 vs. Utah.
facts.why: Sixty-point games are so rare that every one gets remembered; the list does the work.

facts.text: 50-point playoff games: 1 — 50 May 4, 2006 vs. Phoenix.
facts.why: Playoff fifties are the rarest big-stage scoring feat.

facts.text: During his 4-game 50-point streak he scored 65, 50, 60, 50.
facts.why: The individual numbers make the streak feel real.

facts.text: Finals appearances: 7 (5-2) — 1999-00 vs. Indiana (won); 2000-01 vs. Philadelphia (won); 2001-02 vs. New Jersey (won); 2003-04 vs. Detroit (lost); 2007-08 vs. Boston (lost); 2008-09 vs. Orlando (won); 2009-10 vs. Boston (won).
facts.why: A complete Finals résumé in one line; both the wins and losses spark replies.

facts.text: In 37 Finals games he averaged 25.3 points; he scored 30+ in 13 of them and 40+ in 1.
facts.why: Finals-only numbers are what legacy arguments turn on.

facts.text: His best scoring season: 35.4 points a game in 2005-06 — 2,832 points in 80 games.
facts.why: The peak season; fans rank it against other all-time scoring years.

facts.text: Scoring titles: 2 — 2005-06 (35.4; runner-up Allen Iverson 33.0); 2006-07 (31.6; runner-up Carmelo Anthony 28.9).
facts.why: Scoring crowns with the runner-up named; both fan bases engage.

facts.text: Regular-season points from 1996-97 through 2015-16: Bryant led the league with 33,643; next Dirk Nowitzki, 29,491.
facts.why: Across those seasons nobody topped him; Dirk Nowitzki came closest and still finished 4,152 behind, which invites Nowitzki fans to argue.

facts.text: Regular-season field goals from 1996-97 through 2015-16: Bryant led the league with 11,719; next Dirk Nowitzki, 10,392.
facts.why: Across those seasons nobody topped him; Dirk Nowitzki came closest and still finished 1,327 behind, which invites Nowitzki fans to argue.

facts.text: Regular-season free throws made from 1996-97 through 2015-16: Bryant led the league with 8,378; next Dirk Nowitzki, 7,006.
facts.why: Across those seasons nobody topped him; Dirk Nowitzki came closest and still finished 1,372 behind, which invites Nowitzki fans to argue.

facts.text: Regular-season minutes from 1996-97 through 2015-16: Bryant led the league with 48,643; next Kevin Garnett, 48,119.
facts.why: Across those seasons nobody topped him; Kevin Garnett came closest and still finished 524 behind, which invites Garnett fans to argue.

facts.text: Playoff points from 1996-97 through 2015-16: Bryant led the league with 5,640; next LeBron James, 5,572.
facts.why: Across those seasons nobody topped him; LeBron James came closest and still finished 68 behind, which invites James fans to argue.

facts.text: Playoff field goals from 1996-97 through 2015-16: Bryant led the league with 2,014; next Tim Duncan, 1,975.
facts.why: Across those seasons nobody topped him; Tim Duncan came closest and still finished 39 behind, which invites Duncan fans to argue.

facts.text: Seasons averaging 30 from 1996-97 through 2015-16: Bryant 3 (2002-03, 2005-06, 2006-07); everyone else combined 11.
facts.why: "Him vs. the league" framing; the count against the field is the post. 3 of 14 such seasons belonged to one player.

facts.text: Seasons averaging 35 from 1996-97 through 2015-16: Bryant 1 (2005-06); everyone else combined 0.
facts.why: The rarest scoring air of his era. One player matching or beating the rest of the league combined is the hook.

facts.text: 60-point regular-season games: Bryant 6, Jordan 4.
facts.why: The rarest scoring nights, compared directly.

facts.text: Regular-season scoring average: Bryant 25.0, Jordan 30.1.

facts.text: Playoff scoring average: Bryant 25.6, Jordan 33.4.
facts.why: Playoff scoring is where the debate is decided for many fans.

facts.text: Titles (derived from playoff results): Bryant 5, Jordan 6.
facts.why: Rings, the first argument in any GOAT thread.

facts.text: Longest run of consecutive playoff games with 30+: 6 (Apr 30, 2010 to May 17, 2010).
facts.why: Playoff scoring streaks feed the big-game argument.

facts.text: His teams' record when he scored 40+ in the regular season: 82-40.
facts.why: Winning when he scored big answers the "ball hog" critique.

facts.text: Bryant reached 25,000 regular-season points in his 990th game, Jan 21, 2010 at Cleveland, at 31 years.
facts.why: Getting there this young is the longevity-plus-production case in one line.

facts.text: Bryant reached 30,000 regular-season points in his 1,180th game, Dec 5, 2012 at New Orleans, at 34 years.
facts.why: The 30K club is tiny; the date and game count make it trivia.

facts.text: Bryant reached 33,000 regular-season points in his 1,310th game, Jan 7, 2016 at Sacramento, at 37 years.
facts.why: The last big milestone of the career; farewell-season content.

facts.text: Christmas Day: 16 games, 24.7 points a game, 6-10; high 42.
facts.why: Post it on Christmas, the league's showcase day.

facts.text: His Finals high: 40 points, Jun 4, 2009 vs. Orlando (W).
facts.why: The biggest night on the biggest stage.

facts.text: In his 5 title-clinching games he scored 26, 26, 25, 30, 23.

facts.text: Game 7s: 5-1, averaging 22.2 points (25 vs. Portland 2000; 30 vs. Sacramento 2002; 24 vs. Phoenix 2006; 14 vs. Houston 2009; 23 vs. Boston 2010; 17 vs. Denver 2012).
facts.why: Game 7 résumés decide legacies in fans' minds.

facts.text: His highest-scoring postseason (10+ games): 32.1 points a game over 12 games in 2002-03.
facts.why: A peak run fans can compare with any star's best.

facts.text: Through 2025-26 he ranks 4th in career regular-season points, passed since retiring by LeBron James.
facts.why: Where he stands today; the name that passed him starts the debate.

facts.text: Seasons in which Bryant and Shaquille O'Neal both averaged 20: 5 — 1999-00 (22.5 and 29.7), 2000-01 (28.5 and 28.7), 2001-02 (25.2 and 27.2), 2002-03 (30.0 and 27.5), 2003-04 (24.0 and 21.5).
facts.why: Duo content always travels; each season invites comparisons with today's pairs.

facts.text: Postseasons of 10+ games averaging 30 from 1996-97 through 2015-16: Bryant 4 (2002-03, 2007-08, 2008-09, 2011-12); everyone else combined 12.

method: Kobe Bryant: every line is computed from stats.nba.com — his career feed, every game he played, and every NBA player-season for league comparisons. Titles and Finals are derived from his playoff game logs. Nothing typed in from memory.
Scoring titles use the rule of each season (70 games or 1,400 points through 2012-13; 58 games after). 'Why' notes are editorial: why the line should work as a post.
